utterances.text: Now, is it correct that Colonel Budimir never informed you that Major Juric was his commander?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't need to, since I was present then --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, my question to you is: Did Mr. Budimir -- or is it correct that Colonel Budimir never informed you that Major Juric was his commander? Not about your impressions. My question is whether Mr. Budimir ever told you that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Mahindaratne, you're creating confusion. Your question was whether it was correct that he never informed him. And now in your next question, you say: My question is whether Mr. Budimir ever told that you that, which is in contradiction with your question. Let me -- that's a different question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me ask again, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so and we expect you, Mr. Milas, to give an answer to what is asked, whether there was any need to do A, B, or C, fine. The question was whether A, B, or C was done. And Ms. Mahindaratne will now put the question in a rephrased way to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Milas, that Colonel Budimir never told you, never informed you, that Major Juric was his commander?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, Your Honour. That he never informed me? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he ever say, and I give you to options, to you: Juric is my commander, or did he never say anything of the kind; that is, that Juric was his commander. Did he or did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He never told me that. The order was clear and there was no need it repeat it to me, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether there was a need, I invited you to refrain from introducing that. Your question [sic] simply is that he never told you that, and you have already stressed several times that the order was clear to you, so there's no need to give this as a further explanation. The Chamber has heard your answers and, even without repetition, will carefully consider your evidence. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, may I have D850, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milas, your testimony was that the other officer who came down with Major Juric, Ante Glavan, was considered as your commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could move to page 46 in the English version -- before that --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Milas? This is a crime report, the annual report of the criminal section of the 72nd Military Police Battalion, dated 31st December, 1995, which is compiled by you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you want to see the signature page? Perhaps if you could go down on the Croatian version, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you notice, that is a report issued by you?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if you could move to page 46 of the English version and 29 of the Croatian version. And there you're reporting on the activities of the crime section of the 72nd Military Police Battalion for the year. And you record as this: "I wish to add that while carrying out their assignments, during the operation and afterwards, members of the military crime investigation police received unselfish professional and personal help from members of the military crime investigation department Ante Glavan and Ante Cicvaric." Now that was reported by you; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. This is the annual report of the crime military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, these are the other two gentlemen who came down with Major Juric from the military police administration. And in reporting that they extended help to the crime section of the 72nd Military Police Battalion, is consistent with my proposition to you, which was that they were sent by the military police administration as coordinators to assist in the work of the military police of the 72nd Battalion; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards Major Juric, the answer is no. As for Ante Glavan and Ante Cicvaric, one could interpret it in such a way, because if Ante Glavan came from the crime military police department and when, under orders, he arrives in another formation, such as the 72nd Battalion, in professional terms, in a way, he becomes my superior, professionally; but also, professionally he is there to assist me. To draw a parallel or an example, we can take the Varivode operation when the chief of the crime military police administration, Spomenko Eljuga, pursuant to General Lausic's order, became a member of the team, and automatically when in the field, he becomes my superior as well as the superior of all those working on the various segments of the crime military police. When someone from that level is in the field, they are our superior. To conclude, this is the annual report drafted and signed by me. It includes the whole period.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: But it is correct, isn't it that what you -- when you refer to Ante Glavan, you don't describe him as the commander in this report, the commander of the crime section, but as a member sent from the professional chain to assist in your work; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say here that he was the chief of the crime military police at that point because that was my post. Much as in the operation of Varivode, it didn't say that the chief of the crime military police --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, if you could confine your response to my question. My question was: You do not report him as commanding your section but as assisting your section. That is my question.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what is stated here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Milas, if General Gotovina issued an order to you to carry out any activity relating to crime prevention, an investigation, would you have -- would you have refused to implement that order?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a hypothetical question. General Gotovina never issued such an order.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, please, you have been asked by the Court to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, Ms. Mahindaratne. It is a hypothetical question. Of course, you could ask the witness whether, if such an order would be given, whether there would be any legal impediment or any practical impediment for him, and then I take it he will describe the structure. But, of course, the problem with hypothetical questions is that you are talking about "an order." What order would that be? But, therefore, I've -- I do agree with the witness that it's hypothetical and would take half an hour to give all the ins and outs on what might have been the considerations if such -- if an order, of whatever kind, would have been put to him by Mr. Gotovina. I invited you earlier to put focussed questions to the witness. I repeat that invitation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me ask you this way, Mr. Milas. In the crime prevention section of the 72nd Military Police Battalion, being the head of crime section, was -- was there any impediment to implementing an order received from the Military District Commander directly or -- either via Colonel Budimir? Was there any problem in implementing such an order?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the two different segments of the military organisation, that would have been extraordinary. One section is the Military District; the other the military police. That would have been unusual. If there were orders to be issued by General Gotovina, he would have done that to Mr. Budimir, in terms of relationship between the Military District and the military police, because General Gotovina was a general of the Croatian army and the commander of a Military District. He issues orders to the commanders of units.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So, if, for instance, General Gotovina has to issue orders to the -- I'm sorry, let me rephrase that. So let me ask this question: Isn't it correct that General Gotovina had the authority to issue an order to the military police to arrest any person he wished to have arrested, if that was required?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What would be the basis for General Gotovina to issue an order to arrest anyone? Arresting needs to be preceded by certain legal pre-conditions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me show a document, in fact, on that, Mr. Milas.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I could have P71, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm going show you an entry, Mr. Milas, from the war diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could go to the Croatian version, page 46, and the English version, page 83.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could the witness's other microphone be switched on as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, this is a record of a working meeting between General Gotovina and his subordinates, subordinate commanders. And do you note that order where General Gotovina says: "Write an order for the commander of the ZM Split Garrison and arrest him." Do you see General Gotovina issues an order to have --

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I apologise. I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you see it now? It's at page 46 of the Croatian version. On to the left -- no, if you could move to the page to -- yes, that's correct. Do you see that this is an -- in small text reference to General Gotovina, and right in front of that, an entry where General Gotovina wants the Split Garrison commander arrested. Do you see that, Mr. Milas?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now that order would have to be issued to the military police, isn't it, because that would be the organisation within the military which could arrest an officer.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see here that an order was issued to the military police. It literally says "write an order to the commander of the Split Garrison and arrest him." I don't see it anywhere that it says that an order was issued to the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas --

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: -- is that an order from General Gotovina or isn't that an order from General Gotovina? How do you read that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't think that is what the witness is indicating, and I'm looking at it myself, and there is some confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the witness is invited to explain how he reads this, which he started doing already. And more specifically Ms. Mahindaratne would like you to reflect on whether this entry refers to an order by General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could you answer my question, Mr. Milas?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it says General Gotovina, I read out the sentence, and I don't know what it is that I'm supposed to comment on. There was no order issued to the military police. It may have been issued to the security service, or maybe a SIS employee, as an authorised official was present at the meeting; and it may be that General Gotovina asked the SIS employee to arrest someone, although I don't see who and for what reason. I can't see it here. That is my only comment because I can tell you that those working for the security service had the right powers and could implement this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me move on, due to lack of time, Mr. Milas. Now, isn't it correct that the crime section of the 72nd Military Police Battalion maintained registers, crime registers?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And every time a criminal report was filed, the report would be designated as what is known as a KU number; isn't that correct?

utterances.text: That was the rule.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, there was a central system within the 72nd Military Police Battalion, isn't that correct, which assigned certain batches of KU numbers to specific companies. utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, for instance, if the company exhausted the number of -- if they exhausted their assigned lot, they would then ask for addition numbers from the central system; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, now, each company had their own crime registers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each company kept its own register.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Whereas, in the case of the Knin Independent Company, because of the nature of its formation, which was a temporary formation, their KU numbers or their criminal reports were entered into the battalion crime register; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot either confirm or deny this because these registers were kept by administrators, and I'm not much familiar with that part of the activity. But I can't deny that what you said was true.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, through the KU numbers, isn't it correct that one could assess the number of crime reports registered for a specific period?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would, among others, be a way to find that out.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And when you say "among others," the others would be the corresponding reports themselves, not just the register, but the register taken with the corresponding crime reports would allow a person to arrive at the number of crime reports filed by a company for a specific period of time; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every case had its own folder, as for a file, with a classification designation and a KU reference. But, as I said, this part of work was handled by administrators. utterances.text: If I could have 7296, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milas, --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have A3, the charts reproduced on A3 charts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't think that -- that was not my understanding of the 13. I thought -- just for the, record, Mr. President, I understood it that you were referring to the lotting committed between August and 30th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The 13 are the crime reports raised which is relevant to the subject matter of this case.

utterances.text: I think you have repeated what had I said, so ...

utterances.text: Well, then it must be clear, isn't it, Mr. Misetic? There's no confusion whatsoever. If you take to us to one example so that we can see what you are talking about.

utterances.text: Yes, if you -- columns are numbered, apparently. If you give us the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And then from there, there are altogether five entries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So let me just try to understand. The eighth row, the first yes in column 13, is that a reference to looting?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because it says aggravated theft but should we understand aggravated theft to be looting?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is the terminology used in their -- the criminal reports. We have just exactly -- yes, reproduced it as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When I say looting, Mr. President, there are 13 cases of looting for this period reported, but in terms of -- we have assessed the material for all crimes which comes within the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I asked you to take us to an example. We've seep one example now. We -- put your questions to the witness.

utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milas, let me tell you. utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The vast territory we were covering, insufficient staff, the number the reports we were receiving, our engagements around the processing of prisoners of war, and covering cases of deaths of HV members outside of the front line, and there were quite a few of those, the causes of which were suicide, accidental death, et cetera, where all the possible reasons of foul play had to be eliminated before these deaths could be ascertained. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Generally speaking, those would be the major limiting factors. That's to say, factors limiting our work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would apply also to Sibenik. Any objection against admission? Mr. Registrar.

utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.text: This is a summary of all the 19 crime reports filed by the 72nd Military Police Battalion during this period. utterances.text: When you say 19, which period are you referring to?

utterances.text: I'm referring to crimes committed in the period August and September, but these reports have been filed during the course of August to April 1996 -- August 1995 to April 1996?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if it could just be made clear to the witness. There are 19 criminal reports filed that relate to crimes in this case. That doesn't mean there were only 19 filed in total for other matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, these are crimes that we selected, based on what is of interest to the Trial Chamber. utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said before that the number is not an impressive one. However, if we had full information about the number of accounts or the information received about HV members having committed such crimes, and if we had information, I happen to know had a Sibenik had nine deaths in September that fell into the category of deaths outside of the front line. Definitely the number is not a significant one, but it would be good to check how many reports were received by the operative duty officer of the 72nd Battalion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have now told us how many death cases you had to investigate which explains, perhaps, the low number, but you have given an explanation already. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. I also spoke to Mr. Marijan Babic in Zadar with Mr. Damir Simic in Sibenik, and I don't recall who it was, maybe Mr. Perkovic who was, at the time, at the head of the crime service about what why the numbers were as they were, and they simply told me, We did not receive accounts about soldiers, active servicemen having done these crimes. utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I have the document which did not get an exhibit number tendered into evidence and that would be 7298. This has already been assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How we will administratively with a matter is a different point of view. I just received a note which I will try to digest from Mr. Registrar. The document is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what number it gets and what number matches to what, we will put that on the record without confusion as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, you -- your explanation -- one explanation was that the military police did not, in fact, receive notice of crimes and which is why there is such a low level of criminal reports raised. Let me, in fact, show you a document --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if I could have P886.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What you are about to see, Mr. Milas, is the military police log-book for the Knin military police company for the period 11th August to 11th November. Can you tell us at least -- this document indicates entries only from 11th August.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If you could just go to the first page so that witness could look at it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know why there aren't any entries before 11th August? And if you could answer briefly, Mr. Milas.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why the duty service did not set that up for the earlier period.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can we go to English, page 16 and the Croatian version page -- yeah. 03577464, even B/C/S page 16. It's -- Mr. Registrar, you should click on the second batch of the -- in the English version, the second batch which starts with 03577452 ET2. Then in that, page 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see, Mr. Milas, on 23rd August at 8.10, there is an entry, a report of a house on fire close to a police check-point, and the report indicates that it was probably done by a member of the HV. And the only action that is recorded against is that a patrol is sent, and it reports that no one was found at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Perhaps the Chamber might not be able to see the remarks. If the English version could be adjusted in such a way that the column entitled remarks could come on to the screen, in the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There is no record of an investigation being conducted, no record of a criminal report being filed? I'm going to take you to a couple of entries to show you that, in fact, the military police did receive notice of crimes committed by HV, particularly, I'm going to take you through cases of arson, since there is no criminal reports filed against that offence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you could go to, on the same batch, page 44, and in the Croatian version page 32.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You see, this is on 5th September, 1625 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think on the English version you should go down the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There is a record of the -- from Knin police reports, this is MUP officer's report, that the old hospital is on fire and that HV members are not allowing the fire to be extinguished and the action taken is a patrol is sent and it comes back saying it did not encounter HV.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you just move the page so Court could see the English one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No record of an investigation or criminal report being raised? And if I could just take you to two more entries.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE

utterances.text: One second, please. 1725?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, it's 1720.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: For to five houses are on fire. Some HV Croatian army members were seen moving around those. utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar [sic], if we could go to page 55 of the English version and the Croatian, page 38. There is no note at 2010: "Knin police reports on the road towards Stara [sic], uniformed men was seen setting houses on fire." And if you could move, Madam Registrar, that page.

utterances.text: And the military police doesn't take any action because it says: "As it is dark, it is better that the patrols go out tomorrow?" And if you go to the next page you see that, in fact, although with regard to the case of arson, it is recorded that a patrol be sent next day. There is no patrol sent, no action taken at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if you can could just move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So what I'm trying to demonstrate to you, Mr. Milas, is that, in fact, the military police had ample information that crimes were being committed by members of the HV but did not take any action at all, particularly when it came to arson. utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you have shown me four occasions or events that were reported on. As far as I recall, in the first case, it is stated that it is presumed that a HV member set a house on fire. In the last example, it is stated that there were some uniformed persons involved. This does not necessarily mean that they were members of the HV. It is evident from all the four cases that a patrol was dispatched to the site. However, the patrols did not come across any perpetrators. As to whether the crime military police was notified about this fact by the duty service, in a such a way that the crime military police could take up any further investigation, that is something I don't know. The facts are as stated therein, stating that the military police did intervene and that a patrol was dispatched but that no perpetrators were encountered. If at the point of reporting, identity is unknown, it is difficult to assert or establish whether it, indeed, involved a member of the HV and who that person was. That is extremely difficult. I do not exclude the possibility that the crime police was not informed of this case, because, maybe, those in the duty office concluded that no HV members were involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in that last entry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, I'm looking at the clock. How much time -- I encouraged to you finish during this session. How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Ten minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I inquire how much time re-examination would take?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No more than ten minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Five minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, nothing arising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We might get in trouble with the tapes. Yes. That's confirmed. Well, unless the interpreters and transcriber would have a problem, the tape is ten more minute, Ms. Mahindaratne. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now in that last entry that I showed you, Mr. Milas, there isn't even a record of a patrol being sent to investigate the case of arson. So can you explain us to as to why the military police was not taking any action upon receipt of cases of crime being committed by HV?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, I don't know whether any measures were taken. The measure that I see that was taken was the dispatch of a patrol to the site. As for any other further measures, that is something that I can't talk about now because I cannot see any such information from the duty operations service log.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, now, you testified about being involved in the -- the operation OA Varivode, which was an investigation into several incidents of killings, and that was an operation set up at the level of the Ministry of Interior, isn't that correct, where the police administrations requested the assistance of the military police to assist in the investigations?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how it was filed. I can only offer my comments in terms of the order of General Mate Lausic, dating, I believe, the 4th of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, are you aware that in the course of that operation, one of your subordinate officers, Damir Simic, was prevented by his company commander, Captain Mrkota, from carrying out an investigation into the activities of commander of the 113th Sibenik Brigade. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That Damir Simic was prevented from doing this? I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I could call up P1062, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is a report written by Mr. Ante Glavan, where he records that Mr. Damir Simic was, in fact, prevented, and if I could take you to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, page 3 of the English version, and the corresponding page would be page 2 of the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you see the paragraph --

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please enlarge the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If could you quickly read that, I will not read it out, Mr. Milas. That reports that, in fact, Damir Simic was prevented from pursuing this investigation.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the previous page, Madam Registrar, page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what paragraph now?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I could have a minute, Mr. President. Yes, it's page 2 of the English version, and in the Croatian version, it would be the paragraph before -- Madam Registrar, if you could, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There you are. Do you see that, Mr. Milas?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it in the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know this as head of crime investigation section? Were you ever informed about this by Mr. Glavan?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: After reading this, I can tell you that I didn't know about this. I was not informed either in writing or orally by Mr. Simic, ever, as far as I can recall. This would present a grave obstruction in terms of performing his duties. As far as I can recall, he never told me about this. As far as I can see, this is a 2002 document that I have just read.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can we have P203, please. I have just one minute, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One minute. Because I already announced because if the tape stops, no one would know when we would resume. We will resume, once the tape has ended, and we will stop immediately talking, and we'll resume after break at ten minutes past 1.00. You have one more minute, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You will see the document on the -- yes. Now, Mr. Milas, you testified that you went through Kistanje and you did not see, you know, destruction which is consistent with it being widespread. Now if we could go to paragraph 4, Madam Registrar. Now, this is a report sent by Ante Gugic, head of security and information section. Do you see that paragraph 4, Mr. Milas?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if you could go to the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you please read that paragraph 4. Now, you visited Kistanje on the 11th. This is dated 8th. So what you state -- testified before this Trial Chamber is quite inconsistent with what Mr. Gugic is writing to Mr. Susak; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was in the centre of Kistanje with Glavan, Cicvaric and Maduna. I did see a concern number of houses that were set on fire and some showed signs of combat damage. But, at that point in time, I could not see that there was any looting or alcohol consumption, although I do not exclude that possibility. I can only tell you what I saw that day, and we only briefly moved through the centre because we continued onwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My last question to you is: Can you just say briefly how long did you go through -- are you saying you were only in the centre very briefly in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven or eight minutes, not more than that. We stopped in the centre next to a destroyed statue. We had a look at it, there was a monument, and then we moved on towards Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I changed the time when we resume. We will have a break, and we will resume at a quarter past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before that, there is an -- for the record, the exhibits that were not tendered, the three charts, there was the confusion and perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think they were all tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President to be given a mark -- exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have P2552, which is the Knin chart; we have P2553, which is the Zadar chart; then and now the next one, questions were asked about the Sibenik chart, although we had the consolidated document on our screen, the 65 ter 7298, that is the Sibenik chart. That should bear number P2554. Then the next one, 65 ter 7299, if I could call it the consolidated chart, that was admitted into evidence and now bears number P2555.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if I could have Exhibit P20 on the screen, please. English, page 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to pull this exhibit, Mr. Milas, on the screen just to provide context for the video that I'm going to show. That is the admitted testimony of a witness named Edward Flynn, was in Kistanje on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to this -- this is leading the witness. This is showing this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The witness has already testified on number of houses and it's been extensively discussed so there is nothing I'm going to lead him on, in terms of the number of burned houses in Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We didn't know yet it would be limited to the numbers. The witness has testified about the numbers. If you would limit your questions to the numbers of houses then, of course, that is --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, but if putting what another witness has testified to this witness and then asking him questions would amount to leading, this is, after all, the witness being called by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is nothing I'm going to put to him, just the context of what it is that we are about to be seen on the screen next. He is not going to be asked anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are going to show P26, we'll see some of pictures, videos taken during a visit on the 13th of August, 1995, and one witness testified about it in this court. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, now, this video -- sorry, was taken on 13th of August, which, according to your testimony, would have been, I believe, two days after you were present in Kistanje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness said that it was anything between the 10th and the 12th so one or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I picked the middle date [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Either the 10th or the 12th, but in any event, at least one day before -- one day after you were in Kistanje. Mr. Registrar, if we could have Exhibit P26, which is a video taken by Mr. Flynn on the 13th. And, Mr. President, I believe we're going start at 2 minute and 12 second mark. And there won't be any audio.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, is this -- when you see a building that is familiar to you, if you could let us know, if at all. Is this building familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is in the centre of Kistanje close to the monument. I think so. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the monument should be somewhere near this house, whether to the left or to the right or ahead it, yes, this is the intersection in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Stop me when you see a burned house. That house appears to have been -- sorry. I guess I will ask -- the question. But obviously that is a house on fire. Do you recall whether when you were in Kistanje that house had been already damaged or otherwise in the process of being burned?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember at this time, no. Not this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was that one -- do you recall, if you can, at all, if that was one of the homes that you had seen burned prior to the 13th of August?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe. I can't give you a definite answer. The one that was shown to me earlier, I think that I saw that one definitely. And if it's the same direction, then perhaps that was the one. I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, that ... was that burned at the time that you were in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Milas, this appears now that the car has been turned around and going back in the other direction?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that evidence is not here. I don't know on what basis Mr. Misetic read that part out as to this appears the car is turned around going the other direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We can do a comparison, Mr. President. If we can go back to 3:06, please. 3:03. And now if we can go back to 3:23, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go a bit back first to 3 -- slower, please, a little bit back, please. Stop there, yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now if we could go to up to 3:23, please. And if we can just let the rest of the video go, please. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, now, other than what we've seen on the screen, do you recall any other -- seeing any other areas of Kistanje that had been set on fire?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was in the centre at the start of the footage where you could see the sign-posts. We went on to Obrovac. In other words, we did not drive through Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My final question for you is, did you ever -- were you ever told, was it ever suggested to you, or in any other way communicated to you that you should investigate burnings? You meaning, the 72nd Military Police crime prevention service?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely nobody ever issued such an order or ever -- ever sent such a request. From the crime prevention service. At no point during the military and police Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm reminded to ask you: With respect to the crime of looting, was it ever suggested to you not to process looting?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm -- I'm told that I maybe was not clear in my enunciation. The transcript should read that the question was: Was it ever suggested to you that you shouldn't - meaning, should not - investigate burnings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Just a few, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Milas. I will now show you a document that we looked at a moment ago, that's the military police operations log and ask you to give us a brief comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could I, Mr. Registrar, could I have please P886 on the screen and precisely page 4 on B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly, Mr. Milas, the operations log is a document that was kept in the operations duty service of the military police; is that right.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Various entries were made into that log based on reports received in whatever way, be it in person, over the phone, or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The operations log would also contain entries to the effect of when the piece of information was received, by whom, what it was about, and what was done as a follow-up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the contents of the log.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: To your recollection and based on your experience, were entries made to the operations log to the effect that any investigation has been launched against a perpetrator, that an indictment has been issued against a perpetrator, and everything else that will follow up once a crime investigation was under way?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's, in fact, what the pre-typed columns of the log envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In other words when my learned friend asked you and asserted that the operation log did not contain entries about criminal reports being filed or investigations carried out, this isn't something that would normally have been entered into the log to begin with; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: At the start of your testimony, what was mentioned was that while witnesses were being proofed at Lora base, members of the SIS of the Republic of Croatia provided certain services, and you said that these were services merely of a technical nature. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm, Mr. Milas, that similarly, similar or identical services were provided to the investigators of the OTP, when they interviewed witnesses?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Lora.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, you just said at the start of your testimony, apparently you were referring to the start of the cross-examination. It comes a bit as a surprise, although we're not bound by the common law tradition, that where you have chosen not to cross-examine this witness that you now take the opportunity to put questions to the witness on matters which were raised in cross where you were in a position to cross-examine the witness yourself on any matter. It comes as a bit of a surprise. I didn't hear any objections by Ms. Mahindaratne. I consulted with my colleague, who is more -- who was educated in the common law tradition. So, therefore, it comes as a bit as of a surprise, Mr. Mikulicic, that you start examining the witness on matters which were not dealt with by Mr. Misetic even objected against the time spent on that, and that you now suddenly jump in, to say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just want to the state that Mr. Mikulicic and I discussed this, and he was going to address the matter since both he, personally, and I, personally, felt called out by Ms. Mahindaratne on certain portions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, of course, your agreement on how to deal with the matter should not interfere with what is the ordinary course of examination of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. But unfortunately, I don't think Mr. Mikulicic could have anticipated prior to the cross-examination, that that was going to be an area for him and me to address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But if you agreed on who would cover what, then you could have addressed the Chamber and said that Mr. Mikulicic seeks leave to put further questions and then give the reasons for that instead of just jumping up and -- at least not in accordance with the usual order. I am not going to stop you at this moment, Mr. Mikulicic, but I would like to ask you to be brief on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will be, Your Honour. My examination was triggered exclusively by the cross-examination of Ms. Mahindaratne, and I raise the theme that was not subject of the direct examination of Mr. Misetic. So I will be very brief, Your Honour. Mr. Registrar, could I have 65 ter 7288 on the screen, please, just the front page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Milas, you are -- do you know the person called Robert Augustincic, Captain Robert Augustincic?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber where it is you now him from, how come you know him and what his job is?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know a person called Robert Augustincic, who is a member of the military security agency and assigned to the intelligence administration of the Main Staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For my information, is this the document we prevented Ms. Mahindaratne from further putting to the witness and now you just call it up as if nothing had happened, as if we had not a thorough decision on --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wouldn't go into the subject of this document. This is not point of my interest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: My point of interest is the person who were present at the examination of the witness by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can ask the witness about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But earlier, we made clear that since this is not evidence, since this was not introduced, since there was no opportunity to put any questions to the author of this document as to its accuracy or the person who gave the statement, that we should refrain from using this document and the first thing you are now doing is to use it. You can ask the witness about what a -- and then the parties could compromise on the matter [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Your Honour, I think my point of using this document is complete different than the point that was used by the Prosecution. I'm using this document, only the front page, just to show that the person working for the SIS was present at the examination of the witness, as he was present in the examination when Defence was interrogating the witness. That is my point, nothing else, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could have asked whether the witness know this is person and then you could have sought ways to have the cover page admitted into evidence, or to agree with the Prosecution that this was a person who has been present at a moment where Mr. Budimir was interviewed. Even if you have different purposes, I think the objection was more fundamental, that is, that there was no opportunity to question anyone about this document, nor the person interviewed, nor the person who put this statement on paper. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are willing to stipulate that Mr. Augustincic was present during this interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And then have you put --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That he was a member of the SIS?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: We do not know that Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... that's a question you -- that's exactly what I suggested without using the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm perfectly happy with that, and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, I think the question on the activities of Mr. Augustincic have been answered. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Kinis has one or more question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, I have short -- two short questions. Referring back to your statement, D1533, paragraph 12. In the bottom -- in the end or last line of this paragraph, you -- you stated is that -- actually, the discussion is about situation when Brigadier Biskic issued a task to secure the depth of area with newly liberated areas. And subparagraph (e) mention to travel only via the main roads, to avoid side roads and shortcuts when travelling by night. Could you, please, more elaborate on this issue, why you should avoid side roads and not travelling during the night?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Brigadier Biskic indicated this because in quite a few places on side roads and country lanes, the roads were mined back at the time when the area was occupied, and in view of what happened on the 11th of August, 1995, when, in the area of Derala [phoen] during the counterattack of the enemy over 20 members 141st Brigade of Croatian army were killed and a great many wounded, the intention on the part of Mr. Biskic was that the entire area was unsafe because of the mines and explosives left behind and possible enemy stragglers. That's my opinion, that that was the reason why he said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: And following to this issue, I wanted to ask you, whether -- deployment of military forces were only along main roads and cities or -- or HV forces were also deployed in some remote areas at that time, in ...

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police performed their duties primarily in the areas that were liberated at large intersections, wherever there were roads. As for the -- or liberated area into the depth, security assessments had to be made. One had to establish where the camps of the enemy forces were and tasks had to be done by way of patrols.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem with the transcript. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The main transcript is working, Your Honour, I think it is the one on the individual screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If everyone uses the LiveNote button so as to be able to follow the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: I'm not asking you regarding enemy forces. I'm asking about HV forces, which discipline you should -- should control, actually.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the witness said camps of Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I said because members of the Croatian army changed their camps. They went into the depth of the liberated areas, and the military police was tasked with following the movements of the Croatian army, and that's what I referred to in my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: That means that all this military forces are only deployed along main roads and cities and not in remote ares like villages or which are connected with side roads.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, we were not stationed in small villages. Rather, in those places where there were command headquarters of Croatian army. I'm saying, as far as I know because I was not involved in that part of the operation, and I'm -- in my answer, I'm actually referring to my experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next question is following paragraph, paragraph 13, you are talking about tasks which was issued in meeting in Knin, pertain to handling war booty. Did you get some instructions what consists war booty, and how you should handle it?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, at the meeting on the 12th of August in Knin, One of the points made by Brigadier Biskic was that the war booty should, obligatory be handed over to the logistics bases of the Croatian army. That stuck in my memory, that bit about war booty but nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: By directly consists war booty or window-frames or stoves or fridges or televisions, et cetera. All it's possible to recognises war booty.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: TV sets would definitely not be considered war booty but certain machinery, larger vehicle, trucks, loaders, roughly along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I keep it very short, Mr. Milas. One question you referred to the experience you had 141st Brigade where you said 20 people were killed and many were wounded. Were they victims of mined roads or ...

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Your Honour, they were killed in a counterattack by enemy sabotage units in the area of Derala. This is the road leading from Knin via Strmica to Grahovo. I'm not a military expert. I can't give you a precise answer, but what was involved was solely the counterattack and enemy fire at closer range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So not mines on roads primarily.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that specific case, no, again, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One last question. A lot has been said about the role of Mr. Juric as being in command or as a coordinator. Since he has been in the area only for a short while, could you tell us specific actions he commanded over which were not to be qualified as coordination activities? What kind of operations or orders or specific matters he dealt with, as far as you remember, which could not be considered to be activities of a rather coordinative nature.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not meet Mr. Juric, save for the meeting on the 3rd of August. I was not present in any -- at any other meetings in which he may have issued separate tasks to anyone. I had more contact with Mr. Glavan and Cicvaric when we toured the employees of the crime military police, and we limit the ourselves to that part of work of the crime prevention section. Mr. Glavan was particularly tasked with POWs, in the sense that he had to report to the MP administration on the number of POWs processed on a daily basis. I didn't have extensive contacts with Mr. Juric. I didn't -- I was not familiar with his daily activities and schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what you said about his tasks was primarily based on the decision by which he was appointed, but you had no direct sight on how he performed his functions and what was where the focus or emphasise exact was.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only refer to the order by General Lausic, nothing beyond that because I was not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. I have no further questions for you, Mr. Milas. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, for answering questions that were put to you by the parties and questions that were put to you by the Bench, and I'd like to wish you a safe trip home again. Before we adjourn, I would first like to express my gratitude to interpreters and transcribers for this additional ten minutes, which allowed the witness to be further excused. We will resume tomorrow, 26th of June, at 9.00 in the morning, in Courtroom I, where we will have a hearing on the motion for the Chamber to issue a restraining order, whereas the -- we resume evidence to be heard Tuesday, the 30th of June, after tomorrow, at 9.00 in the morning at -- in Courtroom III. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one question, is it necessary that our clients should be present tomorrow at the hearing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If he prefers not to be present, we have a rather technical hearing on a matter which is primarily of a legal nature and not the core of the substance of this case. So if you were -- if Mr. Markac and/or Mr. Gotovina or Mr. Cermak would choose not to be present, then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Our client says that doesn't want to be prevent either. If he could be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if I understand well, all three accused then prefer not to be present --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- tomorrow in court, and that is acceptable for the Chamber. So it's just a matter of organizing and transportation, et cetera, is cancelled as well. Any other matter? Then we adjourn until tomorrow, 26th of June, 9.00, Courtroom I.
